alt.en: A black and white photograph of a large two-and-a-half-storey brick house, its front painted white and its side bare brick, with a small bell tower and a television aerial on the roof, an iron fire escape across the front, bushes and a wire fence below and a tree at the right.
alt.es: Fotografía en blanco y negro de una gran casa de ladrillo de dos plantas y media, con la fachada pintada de blanco y el costado de ladrillo visto, un pequeño campanario y una antena de televisión en el tejado, una escalera de incendios de hierro sobre la fachada, arbustos y una cerca de alambre abajo y un árbol a la derecha.

caption.en: The South Family's dwelling house in the Shaker village at Watervliet, New York, photographed in 1962: the home of a Shaker family in the years of the revival that broke out in the fall of 1837.
caption.es: La casa de la South Family en la aldea shaker de Watervliet, Nueva York, fotografiada en 1962: el hogar de una familia shaker en los años del avivamiento que estalló en el otoño de 1837.

source: Historic American Buildings Survey, June 1962, FROM SOUTHWEST. - Shaker South Family Dwelling House, Watervliet Shaker Road, Colonie Township, Watervliet, Albany County, NY (HABS NY-3261); Jack E. Boucher, photographer (detail: the right-hand part of the view)

alt.en: A printed book plate headed Salix babylonica, The Babylonian, or Weeping, Willow: a young tree whose branches hang down like a curtain, marked 19 ft. high, 4 in. diam., with drawings of a leafy twig, a bare drooping shoot and two large leaves below.
alt.es: Lámina impresa de un libro, titulada Salix babylonica, The Babylonian, or Weeping, Willow: un árbol joven cuyas ramas cuelgan como una cortina, con la nota 19 ft. high, 4 in. diam., y debajo dibujos de una ramita con hojas, un brote colgante sin hojas y dos hojas grandes.

caption.en: A weeping willow drawn for J. C. Loudon's book of trees, printed in London in 1838. "Who will bow and bend like a willow", the song begins: a willow bends low in the wind and springs back.
caption.es: Un sauce llorón dibujado para el libro de árboles de J. C. Loudon, impreso en Londres en 1838. "Who will bow and bend like a willow" (¿quién se inclinará y se doblará como un sauce?), empieza la canción: un sauce se dobla hasta abajo con el viento y vuelve a enderezarse.

source: J. C. Loudon, Arboretum et Fruticetum Britannicum, vol. 7 (plates; London: Longman, 1838), plate LXII. E, p. 207, "Salix babylonica. The Babylonian, or Weeping, Willow."
library: Wellcome Collection (scan on the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Internet Archive record (contributor Wellcome Library): "This work is available under the Creative Commons, Public Domain Mark" (http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Printed London 1838; Loudon died 1843; the plate is unsigned, and any artist or engraver at work in 1838 died long before 1926, so public domain in the US, the EU, Israel (life plus 70) and Mexico (life plus 100).
